::: {#fig-plateau}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: plateau-size-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the size of the gradient of the function log of 1 plus e to the
#|   minus x, against x from -5 to 15, on a logarithmic vertical axis.
#|   A solid blue curve falls from about 0.99 at x of -5 to about 0.0000003
#|   at x of 15. It is always positive and never reaches 0.
#|   Two vermilion triangles mark x of 0, where the size is 0.5,
#|   and x of 10, where it is about 0.00005.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
plateau_grid_pf <- seq(-5, 15, length.out = 401)
plateau_size_pf <- 1 / (1 + exp(plateau_grid_pf))
plateau_curve_pf <- tibble::tibble(x = plateau_grid_pf, size = plateau_size_pf)
plateau_marks_x_pf <- c(0, 10)
plateau_marks_size_pf <- 1 / (1 + exp(plateau_marks_x_pf))
plateau_marks_pf <- tibble::tibble(x = plateau_marks_x_pf, size = plateau_marks_size_pf)
ggplot2::ggplot(plateau_curve_pf, ggplot2::aes(x, size)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = plateau_marks_pf, colour = "#D55E00", shape = 17, size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "Size of the gradient (log scale)")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: plateau-size-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the size of the gradient of the function log of 1 plus e to the
#|   minus x, against x from -5 to 15, on a logarithmic vertical axis.
#|   A solid blue curve falls from about 0.99 at x of -5 to about 0.0000003
#|   at x of 15. It is always positive and never reaches 0.
#|   Two vermilion triangles mark x of 0, where the size is 0.5,
#|   and x of 10, where it is about 0.00005.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plateau_grid_pf = np.linspace(-5, 15, 401)
plateau_marks_pf = np.array([0, 10])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(plateau_grid_pf, 1 / (1 + np.exp(plateau_grid_pf)), color="#0072B2")
ax.plot(plateau_marks_pf, 1 / (1 + np.exp(plateau_marks_pf)),
        color="#D55E00", marker="^", markersize=8, linestyle="")
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("x")
ax.set_ylabel("Size of the gradient (log scale)")
plt.show()
```

:::

The size of the [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative)
of the function of @exm-plateau,
with the two values of $x$ from the example marked.
It shrinks toward $0$ as $x$ grows but is never $0$,
which is why descent slows down on a [plateau](#def-plateau)
without stopping at a [stationary point](#def-stationary-point).

:::
